question.text: What must you have to drive on a Wisconsin public road, and which tests lead to it?

answer.text: You need a valid driver license to drive on any Wisconsin public road, and getting one means passing a short series of tests: a vision screening, a highway signs test, a knowledge test and a skills test.

teaching.text: Four steps stand between you and a Wisconsin license, and vision comes first, then the two written tests, then the drive. Remember: Vision, signs, knowledge, skills.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You need a valid driver license to drive on any Wisconsin public road, and getting one means passing a short series of tests: a vision screening, a highway signs test, a knowledge test and a skills test.

question.text: What does the vision screening measure, and who can give it?

answer.text: The vision screening measures how well you see, and either the DMV or your own vision specialist can give it.

teaching.text: You can use the DMV or your own vision specialist, and if the screening is failed, the next stop is a specialist with the vision certificate. Remember: DMV or your own specialist.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The vision screening measures how well you see, and either the DMV or your own vision specialist can give it.

question.text: What visual acuity must a regular car or motorcycle applicant reach, and may glasses be worn?

answer.text: Regular car and motorcycle applicants must have visual acuity of at least twenty over forty in one eye, and glasses or contacts are allowed for that reading.

teaching.text: The acuity bar is twenty-forty, it needs only one eye, and glasses or contacts may be worn. Remember: Twenty-forty, one eye, lenses okay.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Regular car and motorcycle applicants must have visual acuity of at least twenty over forty in one eye, and glasses or contacts are allowed for that reading.

question.text: What field of vision must an applicant have, and how is it measured?

answer.text: Applicants must also have a seventy-degree field of vision measured from the center of each eye.

teaching.text: Field of vision is about width, seventy degrees, and it is measured from the center of each eye. Remember: Seventy degrees from each eye.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Applicants must also have a seventy-degree field of vision measured from the center of each eye.

question.text: Which vision rule needs only one eye, and which is measured for each eye?

answer.text: The acuity rule of at least twenty over forty needs to be met in only one eye, but the seventy-degree field-of-vision rule is measured from the center of each eye.

teaching.text: Match the eye count to the rule: one eye for sharpness, each eye for width. Remember: Acuity one eye, field each.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The acuity rule of at least twenty over forty needs to be met in only one eye, but the seventy-degree field-of-vision rule is measured from the center of each eye.

question.text: Does wearing glasses during the acuity reading count against you?

answer.text: The twenty over forty acuity standard may be met with or without corrective lenses, so wearing glasses does not by itself fail the screening.

teaching.text: Corrective lenses are allowed, so a reading taken with glasses still counts. Remember: Lenses count toward the reading.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The twenty over forty acuity standard may be met with or without corrective lenses, so wearing glasses does not by itself fail the screening.

question.text: What does the highway signs test check?

answer.text: The highway signs test checks whether you can read and understand the signs that regulate traffic, warn drivers and give directions.

teaching.text: The signs test is about reading signs, and understanding what each one asks you to do. Remember: Regulate, warn, direct.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The highway signs test checks whether you can read and understand the signs that regulate traffic, warn drivers and give directions.

question.text: How many questions are on the highway signs test, and how many must you get right?

answer.text: The highway signs test has fifteen questions, and you must answer twelve of them correctly, which is eighty percent, to pass.

teaching.text: You can miss only three of the fifteen signs questions. Remember: Fifteen asked, twelve right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The highway signs test has fifteen questions, and you must answer twelve of them correctly, which is eighty percent, to pass.

question.text: Do you need an appointment for the highway signs test?

answer.text: You can walk in for the highway signs test without making an appointment.

teaching.text: No booking is needed for the signs test; you can walk in. Remember: Signs test is walk-in.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You can walk in for the highway signs test without making an appointment.

question.text: How much of the signs chapter should you study before the signs test?

answer.text: The handbook covers every type of sign you may meet, and it tells applicants to study all of them before the signs test.

teaching.text: Treat the whole signs chapter as the syllabus, because any sign type can appear. Remember: Study every sign type.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The handbook covers every type of sign you may meet, and it tells applicants to study all of them before the signs test.

question.text: What does the knowledge test measure, and do you need an appointment for it?

answer.text: The knowledge test measures what you know about Wisconsin traffic laws, and you can take it without an appointment.

teaching.text: The knowledge test is about traffic laws, and it is walk-in like the signs test. Remember: Traffic laws, walk-in.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The knowledge test measures what you know about Wisconsin traffic laws, and you can take it without an appointment.

question.text: How many questions are on the knowledge test, and how many correct answers pass it?

answer.text: The knowledge test has fifty questions, and you need forty correct answers, or eighty percent, to pass.

teaching.text: On the knowledge test you can miss up to ten of the fifty questions. Remember: Fifty asked, forty right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The knowledge test has fifty questions, and you need forty correct answers, or eighty percent, to pass.

question.text: Both written tests share one pass bar, so how do their question counts differ?

answer.text: Both written tests use the same eighty percent bar, but the highway signs test is twelve right out of fifteen while the knowledge test is forty right out of fifty.

teaching.text: Same eighty percent bar, but twelve of fifteen for signs and forty of fifty for knowledge. Remember: Same bar, different counts.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Both written tests use the same eighty percent bar, but the highway signs test is twelve right out of fifteen while the knowledge test is forty right out of fifty.

question.text: How does the subject of the signs test differ from the subject of the knowledge test?

answer.text: The highway signs test is about reading signs that regulate, warn and direct traffic, while the knowledge test is about traffic laws.

teaching.text: One written test is about reading signs, the other is about the laws themselves. Remember: Signs versus laws.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The highway signs test is about reading signs that regulate, warn and direct traffic, while the knowledge test is about traffic laws.

question.text: About how long does the knowledge test take, and what does that mean for when you arrive?

answer.text: Expect the knowledge test to take about forty-five minutes, so arrive early enough to finish before the DMV customer service center closes for the day.

teaching.text: Set aside about forty-five minutes and count back from closing time. Remember: Forty-five minutes, come early.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Expect the knowledge test to take about forty-five minutes, so arrive early enough to finish before the DMV customer service center closes for the day.

question.text: Why does the handbook tell you to start the knowledge test early in the day?

answer.text: Because the knowledge test takes about forty-five minutes, the handbook says to start early enough to finish before the customer service center closes.

teaching.text: Arriving close to closing time risks not finishing the test. Remember: Finish before closing time.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Because the knowledge test takes about forty-five minutes, the handbook says to start early enough to finish before the customer service center closes.

question.text: What does it cost to take the tests at a DMV customer service center, and where is a practice test?

answer.text: Taking the tests at a DMV customer service center is free, and the DMV website also offers a free practice test.

teaching.text: In-person testing costs nothing, and a free practice test is on the DMV website. Remember: Free tests, free practice.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Taking the tests at a DMV customer service center is free, and the DMV website also offers a free practice test.

question.text: Which applicants may take the knowledge test online, and what does that cost?

answer.text: Applicants between ages fifteen and seventeen have the option of taking the knowledge test online instead, for a fee of ten dollars.

teaching.text: Only applicants aged fifteen to seventeen get the online route, and it costs ten dollars. Remember: Teens online, ten dollars.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Applicants between ages fifteen and seventeen have the option of taking the knowledge test online instead, for a fee of ten dollars.

question.text: Which way of taking the knowledge test costs money, and which is free?

answer.text: The signs and knowledge tests are free at a DMV customer service center, while the online knowledge test option for ages fifteen to seventeen costs ten dollars.

teaching.text: Free at the center, ten dollars online for the younger age group. Remember: Center free, online paid.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The signs and knowledge tests are free at a DMV customer service center, while the online knowledge test option for ages fifteen to seventeen costs ten dollars.

question.text: For which applicants does the handbook describe the online knowledge test?

answer.text: The handbook mentions the online knowledge test option only for applicants between ages fifteen and seventeen, and that option carries a fee.

teaching.text: The online route is described only for ages fifteen to seventeen. Remember: Online only for younger teens.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The handbook mentions the online knowledge test option only for applicants between ages fifteen and seventeen, and that option carries a fee.

question.text: What is the skills test, and what does it show the examiner?

answer.text: The skills test is the same thing as the road test or driving test: a real-world demonstration that you can keep ordinary, reasonable control of your vehicle.

teaching.text: The skills test is an on-road demonstration of ordinary, reasonable control of your vehicle. Remember: Ordinary, reasonable vehicle control.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The skills test is the same thing as the road test or driving test: a real-world demonstration that you can keep ordinary, reasonable control of your vehicle.

question.text: What are the three names for the on-road exam?

answer.text: The road test, the driving test and the skills test are three names for the same on-road exam with a DMV examiner.

teaching.text: Whichever name you hear, road test, driving test or skills test, it is the same exam. Remember: Road, driving, skills: same.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The road test, the driving test and the skills test are three names for the same on-road exam with a DMV examiner.

question.text: Who rides with you on the skills test, and what do they do?

answer.text: A DMV examiner goes with you on the skills test and gives spoken directions, for example to turn left at the next intersection or to make a Y-turn.

teaching.text: Listen to each spoken direction from the examiner fully before you act on it. Remember: Examiner gives spoken directions.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A DMV examiner goes with you on the skills test and gives spoken directions, for example to turn left at the next intersection or to make a Y-turn.

question.text: Which test needs an appointment, and where do you book it?

answer.text: Unlike the written tests, the skills test needs an appointment, which you book through the road test page of the Wisconsin DMV website.

teaching.text: The skills test is the one test you must book ahead, through the road test page. Remember: Book the road test online.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Unlike the written tests, the skills test needs an appointment, which you book through the road test page of the Wisconsin DMV website.

question.text: Which tests are walk-in, and which one must be scheduled?

answer.text: The two written tests are walk-in, but the skills test is appointment-only and is scheduled on the DMV road test web page.

teaching.text: Written tests are walk-in, while the drive needs an appointment. Remember: Written walk-in, skills booked.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The two written tests are walk-in, but the skills test is appointment-only and is scheduled on the DMV road test web page.

question.text: What happens to your car before the skills test begins?

answer.text: Before the skills test starts, the examiner inspects your car to confirm it is safe to drive, looking at the horn, lights and signals, license plates, doors, mirrors and more.

teaching.text: Check your horn, lights, signals, plates, doors and mirrors before test day. Remember: Examiner inspects the car first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Before the skills test starts, the examiner inspects your car to confirm it is safe to drive, looking at the horn, lights and signals, license plates, doors, mirrors and more.

question.text: On test day, is only the driver checked?

answer.text: The examiner checks the car before any driving starts, looking at the horn, lights and signals, plates, doors and mirrors to make sure it is safe to drive.

teaching.text: A car that fails the inspection can stop the test before it starts. Remember: The car is checked too.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The examiner checks the car before any driving starts, looking at the horn, lights and signals, plates, doors and mirrors to make sure it is safe to drive.

question.text: Which vehicle controls should you be able to work during the skills test?

answer.text: You should know how to work every vehicle control you might need during the test, such as the headlights, the wipers and the defroster.

teaching.text: Find the headlight, wiper and defrost controls before the test, not during it. Remember: Lights, wipers, defroster.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You should know how to work every vehicle control you might need during the test, such as the headlights, the wipers and the defroster.

question.text: Is knowing the headlight, wiper and defrost controls optional for the road test?

answer.text: Knowing where the headlight, wiper and defrost controls are is part of being ready for the road test, not an optional extra.

teaching.text: Knowing the controls is part of being ready for the road test. Remember: Controls are part of readiness.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Knowing where the headlight, wiper and defrost controls are is part of being ready for the road test, not an optional extra.

question.text: Which turning and intersection skills does the skills test grade?

answer.text: The skills test grades turning, intersections where you must stop, and the approach to intersections where no stop is required.

teaching.text: Turns, must-stop intersections and no-stop approaches are all graded. Remember: Turns, stop and no-stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The skills test grades turning, intersections where you must stop, and the approach to intersections where no stop is required.

question.text: Which two kinds of intersections are graded on the road test?

answer.text: Intersections are graded both ways on the road test: the ones where you must stop and the ones you approach without a stop.

teaching.text: Approach a no-stop intersection with the same care as a stop-sign corner. Remember: Must-stop and no-stop both.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Intersections are graded both ways on the road test: the ones where you must stop and the ones you approach without a stop.

question.text: Besides turns and intersections, which other driving skills are graded?

answer.text: It also grades driving through business or residential areas, changing lanes, and backing up.

teaching.text: Plan practice drives through neighborhoods and business areas, with lane changes and backing. Remember: Areas, lane changes, backing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: It also grades driving through business or residential areas, changing lanes, and backing up.

question.text: Which set maneuvers are on the skills test?

answer.text: The test includes set maneuvers such as a Y-turn, a roadside stop and start, and parking, so practice each one beforehand.

teaching.text: Practice the Y-turn, the roadside stop and start, and parking before test day. Remember: Y-turn, roadside stop, parking.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The test includes set maneuvers such as a Y-turn, a roadside stop and start, and parking, so practice each one beforehand.

question.text: In what two ways does the Y-turn show up in the skills test description?

answer.text: A Y-turn appears both as an example examiner instruction and as one of the listed maneuvers, alongside the roadside stop and start and parking.

teaching.text: The Y-turn is mentioned twice, so expect to perform one. Remember: Instruction and listed maneuver.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Y-turn appears both as an example examiner instruction and as one of the listed maneuvers, alongside the roadside stop and start and parking.

question.text: How does the handbook say to get ready for the skills test?

answer.text: The DMV website has more guidance on preparing for the skills test, and the handbook advises practicing every listed skill before test day.

teaching.text: Use the DMV website guidance and practice every listed skill ahead of time. Remember: Practice every listed skill.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The DMV website has more guidance on preparing for the skills test, and the handbook advises practicing every listed skill before test day.
